idea-plugin.name: Antigravity CLI Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Runs the Antigravity CLI (agy) in a JetBrains IDE terminal (PhpStorm, IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, PyCharm, GoLand, etc.) and feeds it live editor context over MCP — active file, selection, open tabs, and inspection diagnostics, on demand.

Independent third-party plugin — not Google's official Antigravity extension. Google's own agent installs from JetBrains AI → Settings → Agents and requires IDE 2026.2.1+ — see Google's official setup guide. If you want that first-party agent panel, use it. This plugin has a different purpose: it runs the Antigravity CLI (agy) in an IDE terminal and feeds it editor context over MCP, on IDE 2023.2 and up, with no JetBrains AI dependency.

The plugin runs a small local MCP (Model Context Protocol) server inside the IDE and registers itself in ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json. Whenever agy needs editor context it calls the plugin over MCP — no env vars, no lockfiles, no platform-specific bridges.

Click the Open Antigravity CLI toolbar button (top-right) to launch agy in an IDE-embedded terminal pre-wired to the running project. By default the button focuses the existing Antigravity terminal tab if one is open; enable Always open a new tab in settings to spawn a fresh session on every click.

Exposed MCP tools

  • ide_get_active_editor — current file path, language, cursor, selection, content.
  • ide_get_open_files — every file currently open in an editor tab.
  • ide_get_diagnostics — inspections/errors/warnings for a file.
  • ide_open_file — open a file at an optional line/column.

Artifacts tool window

A right-anchored tool window lists recent brain entries agy generates — plans, summaries, walkthroughs from your conversations. Sorted by most-recently modified so the active session's output is always at the top; the conversation ID prefix on each row helps distinguish entries that share a filename. Auto-refreshes every few seconds while the tab is open; double-click any entry to open it in the editor.

Configure the path to your agy binary under Settings → Tools → Antigravity CLI Companion. No keyboard shortcut is bound by default — assign one via Settings → Keymap (search Open Antigravity CLI) or from the link in the plugin's settings panel.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.6.0

  • New setting: Auto-approve tool calls (skip permission prompts) — off by default. agy ships with its request-review tool-permission mode as the default, which is why it stops to ask before running each command. Ticking this box launches it with --dangerously-skip-permissions instead, so a session runs uninterrupted. It is a launch argument, not a config edit: only sessions started from this IDE are affected, an agy you run in a plain terminal is unchanged, and the plugin still writes nothing to ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json — agy rewrites that file itself, so editing it from the IDE would risk clobbering a hand-curated allowlist. Two things still prompt regardless: admin escalation, and access outside the workspace root (governed by agy's own allowNonWorkspaceAccess). Applies to the next session you open; tabs already running keep the mode they started with.
  • Long setting descriptions no longer run off the edge of the panel: the hints under Always open a new tab and Path to agy executable were plain single-line labels, which Swing lays out without wrapping — the text was simply clipped at the right edge of the dialog (“…spawn a fresh agy session on every c”). They now wrap at the same width as the other hints, as does the WSL2 note on Windows, which had markup but no width to wrap against.

1.5.0

  • Renamed to Antigravity CLI Companion: the old name read as though this were Google's own extension. It is not — it is an independent third-party plugin, published months before any official JetBrains integration existed. Google's own agent installs from JetBrains AI → Settings → Agents and requires IDE 2026.2.1+; this plugin does something different, running the Antigravity CLI (agy) in an IDE terminal and feeding it editor context over MCP on IDE 2023.2 and up, with no JetBrains AI dependency. The settings page is now Settings → Tools → Antigravity CLI Companion; nothing else moves, and existing installs update in place.
  • The Artifacts tool window lists artifacts again: it had been ranking conversations by directory mtime and keeping only the 20 most recent. Current agy creates .system_generated/ (transcripts, per-step output, task logs) at conversation start and writes into it for the whole session, so every busy conversation looked recent whether or not it ever produced an artifact — and each one evicted a conversation that actually held a plan or walkthrough. On a real brain directory the panel was showing 3 of 34 artifacts. Ranking now happens on the artifact files themselves, so the active session's implementation_plan.md or walkthrough.md lands on top the moment it is written.
  • Artifacts: right-click menu: right-clicking an artifact now offers Copy Path and Reveal in Finder / Show in Explorer / Show in Files (the label follows the OS). The click also moves the selection to the row under the cursor, so the menu always acts on the artifact you actually clicked.

1.4.1

  • No longer writes to ~/.terminfo when the workaround is switched off: the terminfo entry was compiled at project open regardless of the Fix prompt editing in the IDE terminal setting, so a user who had turned the feature off — or who never launched agy at all — still got a file written into their home directory. The lookup is now skipped while the setting is off, and runs when it is switched back on.
  • Settings panel no longer stretches sideways: the hint under Fix prompt editing in the IDE terminal was a single-line HTML label, which Swing lays out without wrapping — it pushed the whole Settings → Tools → Antigravity CLI Companion page far wider than the dialog. The text is now shorter and wraps at a scaled width.

1.4.0

  • Prompt editing no longer garbles the terminal: editing in the middle of the agy prompt used to scramble the display — inserted text landed several columns too far right and the tail of the line was duplicated. agy moves the cursor left with CSI Z (cursor backward tabulation), which JediTerm — the emulator behind both the classic and the reworked IDE terminal — parses but does not implement, so the cursor silently stayed put while agy believed it had moved. agy only enables that optimisation when TERM carries an xterm prefix, so the plugin now launches it under an equivalent non-xterm terminal name (a private agyterm-256color entry compiled into ~/.terminfo, falling back to nsterm-256color). The -256color suffix is load-bearing: the IDE terminal exports no COLORTERM, so TERM is the only signal agy has for colour depth, and a name without it silently drops the palette to 16 colours. Nothing else is lost — 256 colours, alt-screen, kitty keyboard and bracketed paste all still negotiate — and the byte cost is unmeasurable. Toggle Fix prompt editing in the IDE terminal under Settings → Tools → Antigravity CLI Companion if you need the terminal name passed through unchanged.

1.3.3

  • WSL2 support documentation: Added notes to the README and Settings UI clarifying that for WSL2 projects, the IDE itself must be run inside WSL (e.g., via JetBrains Gateway) rather than using a Windows-side configuration. (Fixes #9)

1.3.2

  • Artifact Viewer Fix: Explicitly open out-of-project markdown artifacts in the text editor rather than the default Markdown editor with JCEF preview to prevent blank screens (Fixes #7).

1.3.1

  • Keymap link fix: Configure shortcut in Keymap settings… now navigates to Settings → Keymap within the open Settings dialog instead of stacking a second Settings window on top.

1.3.0

  • Reuse Antigravity tab: the toolbar action (now Open Antigravity CLI) focuses the existing Antigravity terminal tab if one is open instead of spawning a new one on every click. Toggle Always open a new tab under Settings → Tools → Antigravity CLI Companion to restore the previous behaviour — multiple parallel agy sessions remain fully supported by the MCP bridge.
  • Keyboard shortcut: the settings panel now shows the current shortcut for Open Antigravity CLI and links straight to Settings → Keymap for assignment. No default is bound — no chord is safe across every JetBrains keymap, so the choice is left to you.

1.2.0

  • Multi-IDE Support: Generalised branding and internal identifiers to support the full JetBrains IDE family (IntelliJ IDEA, PhpStorm, WebStorm, PyCharm, GoLand, etc.).
  • Critical Fix: Prevented destructive overwriting of mcp_config.json when the file is malformed (Fixes #3).
  • UI Polish: Properly centered and scaled the plugin icon.

1.1.0

  • Artifacts Tool Window: New right-anchored panel to view and open plans, summaries, and walkthroughs generated by agy.
  • Shell Environment: agy now launches within a login/interactive shell for proper PATH inheritance on macOS and Linux.

1.0.1

  • Replaced the deprecated TerminalToolWindowManager.createLocalShellWidget(...) call with the non-deprecated createNewSession(runner, TerminalTabState) path.
  • Replaced the deprecated 4-arg TextFieldWithBrowseButton.addBrowseFolderListener(...) in the settings panel with the modern TextBrowseFolderListener form.
  • agy now runs as the terminal tab's process directly; the tab closes cleanly when the user exits agy.

1.0.0

  • Initial public release.
